target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable prompt-cache churn when Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` interleave with normal session turns.

The user-visible symptom from redacted live traces was that otherwise similar same-session turns alternated between mostly uncached prompts and much smaller cached prefixes, even though the session-level visible-reply contract was configured as automatic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Strict room-event delivery stays unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual visible delivery and `forceMessageTool`.

The fix separates the prompt-facing delivery mode from the effective delivery mode, then forwards that prompt-facing mode through both queued embedded-runner paths. System-prompt construction can now use the session-stable mode while actual room-event output remains message-tool-only.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

Owner-only core Gateway tools stay prompt-visible for cache stability, but non-owner execution remains blocked by the existing wrapper path.

## User Impact

Room-event turns preserve the same prompt/cache contract as the rest of the session without relaxing message-tool-only delivery. Operators should see fewer avoidable prompt-prefix cache misses when room-event turns interleave with direct or primary session turns.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Original redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Additional redacted live provider traces after the tool-inventory fix showed stable prompt-visible tools:
- Seven same-session GLM-5.2 traces all had `tools=47`, owner-only tools present, and the same tool-list hash `e6f50de5e2`.
- Warm provider cache reads were `46912`, `49408`, `49792`, `49920`, `52224`, and `49856` cached tokens.

Additional redacted trajectory proof after installing `70f05d4ff24` locally:
- Same session, same model family, owner turn then non-owner/bot turn.
- Both turns had `systemOriginalChars=108314`.
- The owner turn reported `lastCallUsage.cacheRead=48640`.
- The immediately following non-owner/bot turn reported `lastCallUsage.cacheRead=49152`.
- This is the previously failing owner/non-owner flip; the system prompt no longer diverged by the old `Current Turn Tool Authorization` block.

Current-head source fix for ClawSweeper's active-session finding:
- `bb4110b4862` forwards `promptSourceReplyDeliveryMode` through `createFollowupRunner` into `runEmbeddedAgent`.
- Regression assertion added in `followup-runner.test.ts` verifies the forwarded value reaches the embedded runner while `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` remains `message_tool_only` and `forceMessageTool` remains true.

Local validation:
- `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps message-tool-only queued followup finals private"` — passed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts --testNamePattern "owner-only tool authorization"` — passed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts --testNamePattern "owner-only core tools"` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were stripped from the evidence before submission.
